reader.requirement: At --std 85 the rule binds the run unit: every FD associated with an external report file connector describes it as a report file; the implementation must translate and run a run unit that obeys it (several separately bound programs each with its own REPORT clause on one EXTERNAL connector, opened OUTPUT or EXTEND), and a run unit that breaks it has undefined results (§1985:I.1.6), so no refusal is required.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.DialectLevel: below 2002 the 1985 FD agreement rows (CheckFileDescriptions), 2002+ the FORMAT rule, 2023 the FILE STATUS/LINAGE external-item rules; none of them concerns the REPORT clause

reader.edition-search: grep for 'report file', IsReport, XIII.3.3.4 across src: no code reads report-file-ness of an external connector; FileEntryIdentity and FileDescriptionIdentity carry no REPORT segment or row.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the conforming run unit runs and the violating one is accepted silently at 85 and at 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf22_06 covers two programs each describing the EXTERNAL file with a REPORT clause, OPEN OUTPUT in the main; EXTEND mode and the violating form are covered only by the probes

probes.expected: the obeying run unit runs with the connector opened EXTEND (OPTIONAL)

reader.notes: Witness g85_bf22_06 MATCHes at 85. The violating run unit compiles and runs silently while the sibling agreement rules of the same connector are refused at compile time by COBOL6847 in ExternalFileConnectorRules.Check; that missing screen is a consistency gap, not a non-conformance, because 1985 leaves the violation's result undefined. No kb/Work note names this rule.

refuter.evidence: I read the reader's run of rce.cob: runs/rce-001/RCEXT.TXT holds MAINLINE then SUB-LINE, so both programs' reports reach the one external connector in order. My probe refute-1985-150/rcw.cob at --std 85 (runs/rcw-001, exit 0) adds report lines of different widths (8 against 20 characters) and OPEN OUTPUT. It also has a main GENERATE after the sub returns, so the sub's INITIATE/TERMINATE runs while RM is active. The file holds MAINLINE / SUB-LINE  WIDER-TEXT / MAINLINE: nothing is truncated, and FileDescriptionIdentity.RecordOf compares nothing for a report FD (it has no record descriptions). This fits §1985:II.3.1. cite.py: OK  §1985:II.3.1  (3.1 REPORT SECTION)  the text is in the clause ('separately compiled programs may specify different reports for the same file-name'). A violating run unit is accepted silently, and the text allows that. cite.py: OK  §1985:I.1.6  (1.6 DEFINITION OF A CONFORMING SOURCE PROGRAM)  the text is in the clause ('The results of violating the formats or rules of Standard COBOL are undefined'). §1985:I.1.5 asks a conforming implementation to flag only syntactically distinguishable extensions. It sets no detection duty for a run-unit general rule. cite.py: OK  §1985:XIII.3.3.4 GR3  (3.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3.
